faq.q: Is it normal to feel like life isn’t what I expected?
faq.a: Yes, it’s very common. Most people carry expectations they absorbed early, and real life rarely matches them exactly. Noticing the gap is a sign of honesty, not failure.

faq.q: Why does it hurt when my life doesn’t match my plans?
faq.a: Because you’re comparing your real life to an imagined one that has no bad days. You may also be grieving a future you were attached to, and that grief is real even if nothing dramatic happened.

faq.q: How do I accept that my life turned out differently?
faq.a: Start by naming the specific expectation, give yourself room to grieve it, and then take stock of what actually showed up. Acceptance grows through small, repeated practices rather than one decision.

faq.q: Does accepting my life mean giving up on my goals?
faq.a: No. Acceptance means you stop fighting reality so you can work with it. You can still want more and move toward it, just without punishing yourself for where you are.

faq.q: How can I stop comparing my life to other people’s?
faq.a: Remember that you’re seeing their highlights, not their full story. Shifting from age-based deadlines to personal directions also makes comparison feel less relevant.

faq.q: What’s a good first step when I feel stuck?
faq.a: Skip the new five-year plan and pick one small action for this week that moves toward the life you want now. Momentum usually brings clarity, not the other way around.
